answer: Comet-Anchor Binding: each identity must continuously hold a unique, operator-owned device key that signs a fresh chained checkpoint over its own local storage history. Enforcement: two identities sharing any device root collide and both get frozen; recovery requires migrating to physically distinct hardware. An attacker scaling to N agents must procure N mutually isolated devices plus their comets of audited history, paying hardware, provisioning, and migration costs per sybil. Cedar and oasis audits let verifiers confirm isolation without exposing keys.
